title: Migration header documents the pre-W4 effective-contact rule; the r1 record W4 in the same diff changes it
evidence: "The sweep and the detail payload read the EFFECTIVE name (corrected_name when present, else contact_name), mirroring the existing corrected_email/corrected_phone treatment." vs "- W4: the effective-contact rule switches to corrected-only once a correction ran (`correction_cycles >= 1`) — a cleared channel never falls back to the proven-dead snapshot (sweep helpers + webhook fallback CASE + client prefill helpers)."
detail: Same PR ships two contradictory effective-contact rules: the migration header keeps the unconditional corrected??snapshot fallback; the r1 record removes that fallback once a correction ran — falling back to a proven-dead contact was the exact W4 defect.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the migration comment to state the corrected-only-once-cycles>=1 rule (or reference the sweep helpers), so a future reader cannot reimplement the W4 defect from the file header.

title: Spec and notes claim the migration adds ONE column; it ships two (corrected_name + corrected_at)
location: spec-rc4-3-row-actions.md (Owns #5, implementation notes, completion notes) vs supabase/migrations/20260812140000_reference_call_corrected_name.sql
evidence: "**`supabase/migrations/`** (expand-only, ONE additive column): `corrected_name TEXT`" / "One expand-only migration: `corrected_name TEXT`" / "Migration: `corrected_name` (expand-only)." vs "ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS corrected_name TEXT," ... "ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS corrected_at TIMESTAMPTZ;"
detail: Three places claim a single additive column, but the migration ships corrected_at too. W3 documents it, so the 'ONE column' claims are stale and now factually wrong in the checked-in docs.
recommended_fix: Amend spec and notes to 'two additive columns (corrected_name, corrected_at)' so the checked-in docs match the shipped migration.

title: Spec Owns #6 omits corrected_name from the additive detail keys the code ships
evidence:
"additive detail keys: `taken_over_at`, `contact_name`, `contact_email`, `contact_phone`, `corrected_email`, `corrected_phone`, `correction_cycles`" vs "#("corrected_name", json.nullable(detail.corrected_name, json.string))" and "use corrected_name <- decode.optional_field(
    "corrected_name",
    None,
    decode.optional(decode.string),
  )"
detail: The payload-contract list omits corrected_name though encoder, decoder, migration and tests all ship it. W4 itself requires client prefill to read corrected values, so the list is stale, not intent.
recommended_fix: Add corrected_name to the Owns #6 additive-key list so the checked-in payload contract matches the shipped code.

title: Back-compat test never asserts the can_take_over default though its wire omits the key
evidence: wire hooks: "\"hooks\":{\"can_record_manual\":true,\"can_substitute_referee\":false,\"can_retry\":false}" ... assertions: "detail.taken_over_at |> should.equal(option.None)" ... "detail.correction_cycles |> should.equal(0)" — no assertion on detail.hooks.can_take_over
detail: The one RC4.3 hook key absent from the old-server wire is exercised but never asserted: if the decoder default flipped to True this test still passes, silently exposing the takeover affordance to old-server users.
recommended_fix: Assert detail.hooks.can_take_over equals False in the missing-keys test and mention the hook key in its doc comment.

title: corrected_at gains a consumer (W3 exhaustion gate) but no writer is named anywhere in this diff's spec/records
evidence: "ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS corrected_at TIMESTAMPTZ;" and "- W3: the exhaustion gate compares the failing send's `at` against a new `corrected_at` column (expand-only, same migration)" — while the correct-query description never names a write: "guard + corrected_* + cycle bump + re-arm in ONE update" and "now resets `attempt_count = 0` + clears `form_token`/`form_token_expires_at`"
detail: If correct_reference_call.sql never stamps corrected_at, every gate comparison is NULL, stands down, and the AD-7 live second-failure terminal never fires. The write site is load-bearing yet undocumented in every spec record.
recommended_fix: Confirm correct_reference_call.sql sets corrected_at = now() on correction and name that write in Owns #4/B1 so the dependency is explicit.
